tasks.locator: Abstract › Data Abstraction (p. 144); Introduction, 3rd paragraph (p. 144); Methods › Outcomes (p. 144, continuing on p. 145)
tasks.extracted: The review states that it abstracted data from prospective controlled trials with methodologically sound end points corresponding to the DSM-IV definitions, and lists withdrawal delirium as defined in DSM-IV among its outcomes; it does not say how the definitions used in its trials, all from before DSM-IV, were judged to correspond. The guideline does not address patients seen after a withdrawal seizure or with established withdrawal delirium (delirium tremens), or the choice of inpatient or outpatient setting.

Withdrawal from trials because of adverse events was more frequent with naltrexone than with placebo, NNH 48 (95% CI 30 to 112; 17 trials, n = 2743); those on naltrexone also had a higher risk of dizziness (NNH 16), nausea (NNH 9) and vomiting (NNH 24).

Editors' arithmetic from the trials' arms in Figure 3: COMBINE contributes 612 of the 1141 (303 on acamprosate, 309 on naltrexone), Mann 2013 341, Morley 2006 108 and Kiefer 2003 80; COMBINE's naltrexone arm is in the review's higher oral dose group, the other three trials' arms in its main dose group.
